post.description: For each asset (fqn + entityType), returns the knowledge linked to it: glossary terms from asset and column tags, metrics applied to it, and articles about it. Deliberately lightweight (no profile, lineage, or budgeting; item content capped) so search layers can annotate a whole result page in one call. Assets and knowledge items the caller cannot view are skipped.

requestBody.description: Assets to resolve, as {fullyQualifiedName, entityType} pairs

post.summary: Batch-resolve the knowledge attached to a set of assets

get.description: REST surface of the find_context MCP tool. Runs a semantic search over the knowledge layer (glossary terms, metrics, articles) and returns the matching definitions together with the candidate data assets each item routes to (glossary terms via tag usage, metrics via APPLIED_TO, articles via HAS). Knowledge items and candidate assets are filtered to those the caller can view.

parameters.description: Natural-language question to find knowledge for
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Maximum knowledge items to return
parameters.name: size

200.description: Knowledge items and the candidate assets they route to

get.summary: Find company knowledge relevant to a question, routed to candidate assets

get.description: Returns a chronological feed of governance-significant events (registered, approved, rejected, assessed, reassessment scheduled, shadow detected). Supports filtering to a single asset via entityType + entityId.
get.summary: Curated AI governance activity feed

get.description: Returns the dashboard widgets in one shot: estate stats, risk × impact matrix counts, framework readiness percentages, top-N Shadow AI detections, top-N pending approvals. Computes from the AI Application / LLM Model / MCP Server entities directly so the UI can render in a single round-trip.
get.summary: Rollup of AI governance state

get.description: Computes the 5 intake checks the Approvals queue surfaces (owner assigned, risk classified, fairness evidence attached, DPIA referenced, transparency disclosure). Each check returns a passing boolean and an evidence reference where applicable.

parameters.description: AI asset type
parameters.name: entityType

parameters.description: Fully qualified name of the asset
parameters.name: fqn

get.summary: Return the AI governance intake checks for an asset

get.description: Returns recent breach events scoped to this policy across the AI estate. Computed by re-evaluating PolicyEvaluator over in-scope AI assets and projecting rule names that match the policy name pattern. Optional since (epoch ms) bound and limit (default 50).
get.summary: Recent breach events for a single AI governance policy

post.description: Bulk register or dismiss a set of Shadow AI detections. 'Register' flips registrationStatus to PendingApproval; 'Dismiss' flips to Rejected with the supplied reason.
Sets registrationStatus to Approved and stamps approvedBy / approvedAt.

get.description: Evaluates a small set of always-on synthetic policies (drift threshold, PII access requires DPIA, subgroup fairness quarterly, human oversight, audit log retention) plus any AIGovernancePolicy entries the asset references. Returns per-rule status: Passing | Breached | NotApplicable.
get.summary: Evaluate AI governance policies attached to an asset

post.description: Sets registrationStatus to Rejected and records the comment.

Convenience endpoint used by the Intake Wizard. Loads the entity, sets registrationStatus to PendingApproval (with registeredBy / registeredAt), and PATCHes back. The intake workflow picks up the change-event and creates a Risk Council approval task.
post.summary: Flip an AI asset's registrationStatus to PendingApproval

put.description:
Update column metadata such as display name, description, tags, glossary terms, and other properties. This API works for the inline children of every supported entity type: table and dashboardDataModel columns, topic and apiEndpoint schema fields, container data-model columns, mlmodel features, pipeline tasks, searchIndex fields and worksheet columns. The column is identified by its fully qualified name and the parent entity type is specified. 

Per-type support:
• description, displayName and tags apply to every type, except displayName on mlmodel features, which have no such property (400)
• constraint and removeConstraint apply to table columns, are ignored for dashboardDataModel, and are rejected for every other type (400)
• extension applies to table and dashboardDataModel columns only (400 elsewhere)

Tag Management Examples:
• Add tags: {"tags": [{"tagFQN": "PersonalData.PII", "source": "Classification"}]}
• Remove specific tag: {"tags": []} (specify only tags you want to keep)
• Remove all tags: {"tags": []}
• Mix classifications and glossary terms: {"tags": [{"tagFQN": "PII.Sensitive", "source": "Classification"}, {"tagFQN": "Glossary.CustomerData", "source": "Glossary"}]}
• Don't change tags: omit the 'tags' field entirely

Validation Rules:
• Invalid or non-existent tags/glossary terms will result in a 404 error
• All tags and glossary terms must exist and be valid before the request succeeds

post.description:
Delete every running process of a Workflow Instance, including one left locked by a server that stopped mid-job, and record the instance as FAILURE. When a job of a periodic-batch trigger instance is executing on this server, a stop request is recorded instead: a batch sink stops before its next sub-batch and the trigger before its next batch, after which the instance is recorded as FAILURE. When a job of any other instance is executing on this server, the termination is refused; retry after it finishes.

A lock held by another server that is still running cannot be told apart from the lock of a server that stopped, so a process whose job another server is executing now is deleted too. For a periodic-batch trigger, the recorded stop request ends that job at its next batch boundary. For any other workflow, that job keeps applying its side effects, such as entity updates, after this call has answered 200.

Each database row-lock wait during the delete is limited to 5 seconds. When a wait runs out, the process is left running and the call answers as for a job executing on this server: 202 with a stop request for a periodic-batch trigger, 409 otherwise. Admin only.

parameters.description: Id of the Workflow Instance
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Reason recorded on the terminated Workflow Instance
parameters.name: reason

202.description: A job of the instance's periodic-batch trigger is executing now; a stop request is recorded and the still running Workflow Instance is returned

404.description: Workflow Instance for `id` not found

409.description: The instance has already ended and has no running process, or a job of its process is executing now and the process reads no stop request or the instance has already ended

parameters.description:
Search Query Text, Pass *text* for substring match; Pass without wildcards for exact match.
1. For listing all tables or topics pass q=*
2. For search tables or topics pass q=*search_term*
3. For searching field names such as search by columnNames pass q=columnNames:address , for searching deleted entities, use q=deleted:true
4. For searching by tag names pass q=tags.tagFQN:user.email
5. When user selects a filter pass q=query_text AND q=tags.tagFQN:user.email AND platform:MYSQL
6. Search with multiple values of same filter q=tags.tagFQN:user.email AND tags.tagFQN:user.address
7. Search by service version and type q=service.type:databaseService AND version:0.1
8. Search Tables with Specific Constraints q=tableConstraints.constraintType.keyword:PRIMARY_KEY AND NOT tier.tagFQN:Tier.Tier1
9. Search with owners q=owner.displayName.keyword:owner_name
NOTE: logic operators such as AND, OR and NOT must be in uppercase

get.description:
Returns per-entity-type counts, a per-connector-type breakdown, an optional per-health-state breakdown, and one page of services sorted by name across every requested service type. Connection configuration is never returned.

Filter semantics: `q` narrows the count maps as well as the list. The three selectors (`listEntityType`, `serviceType`, `health`) narrow only `data` and `paging.total`, so a client can use each count map as the option list for its own filter control without that control eating its own menu.

`offset` + `limit` must not exceed 10000; use the per-service-type list APIs with cursor paging for deeper traversal.

parameters.description: Service entity types forming the universe for the count maps. Repeatable. Defaults to all.
parameters.name: entityType

parameters.description: Restrict `data` to these service entity types. Repeatable. Defaults to the universe.
parameters.name: listEntityType

parameters.description: Connector type, e.g. `Snowflake`. Repeatable. Affects `data` only.
parameters.name: serviceType

parameters.description: Health state. Repeatable. Affects `data` only. Implies `includeHealth`.
parameters.name: health

parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on name and displayName.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Compute per-service health. Costs three extra batched queries.
parameters.name: includeHealth

parameters.description: Sort direction on name.
parameters.name: sortOrder

parameters.description: Fully qualified name of a domain to restrict results to.
parameters.name: domain

parameters.description: Exclude services with this provider, e.g. `system`.
parameters.name: excludeProvider

200.description: Service counts and one page of services

get.summary: Get service counts and one merged, name-sorted page of services
